The anime industry saw a massive change in the animation style with the exceptional hand-drawn cel animation and detailed layouts, before animation studios shifted […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google When it comes to anime classics, t he 1990s was a different era altogether . It was the most revolutionary time for the anime industry since the medium broke into the global mainstream. The anime industry saw a massive change in the animation style with the exceptional hand-drawn cel animation and detailed layouts, before animation studios shifted to digital ink and paint toward the late 1990s. While TV broadcasts were mostly shows suitable for kids, the mainstream anime medium shifted towards darker and more intense storytelling. This was a breakthrough for the anime industry as it became mainstream through older fans.

While the 2020s keep seeing an oversaturation of shows and movies, the 1990s released fewer but iconic anime , most of which are loved even to this day. Anime created during that era were a lot more experimental since they allowed directors and animators more artistic freedom. This is evidenced by the fact that many classics fans love today are still unmatched in terms of both storytelling and animation style. If you haven't already watched these 1990s anime classics, then now is the perfect time to do so.

Yoshihiro Togashi isn't just known for Hunter x Hunter , but he actually made a name for himself in the industry through the Shonen Jump hit, Yu Yu Hakusho . There's no denying that the anime suffered from poor pacing and animation inconsistencies. However, what really matters is that it remains entertaining despite the issues while also having a unique premise that hasn't been replicated even today. The anime began airing decades ago, and even now, not many series can keep viewers hooked as it did.

While the animation isn't flashy, it stands out for its impeccable fight choreography, something Studio Pierrot was unmatched in during the 1990s and 2000s. A huge reason behind the success of this anime is that it killed off its protagonist at the beginning of the story, after which the story took one unexpected turn after another. Whether it's the character development or the world-building, Togashi proved why he is known as one of the greatest creators of all time.

Directed by the legendary Satoshi Kon, the film hit the Japanese theaters in 1998 and eventually became  one of the greatest psychological thrillers  of all time, not just in anime but in all mainstream media. This psychological horror film stands out for blurring the line between reality and fantasy, all the while depicting some of the best visuals seen in the industry. The film’s animation and visual storytelling have never been recreated with modern animation, making it all the more distinctive and memorable.

Not to mention that this film earned Satoshi Kon worldwide recognition, kickstarting his legendary career. The story centers around Mima Kirigoe, who leaves her famous J-pop idol group to pursue her acting career, but before long she gets entangled in a series of strange events that make her question her own sanity. The movie masterfully blends mind-bending storytelling while focusing on the gradual deterioration of Mima’s mental state as she is unable to tell reality from delusion apart. 

Princess Mononoke is pretty much an obvious entry to this list of 1990s anime classics. If you have been an anime fan for quite a while, there's no way you haven't watched any films by Studio Ghibli. The studio’s trademark is hand-drawn animation with exceptional attention to detail, including lush landscapes, fluid movement, and expressive characters featuring visually stunning scenes. Among the many classics from the studio, Princess Mononoke stands out for its darker tone, as it focuses on the moral ambiguity of the main characters.

While Ghibli is known for its whimsical fantasies, this classic depicted intense battle violence all the while portraying the reality of human conflict. Many fans don't even know, but this movie basically saved Ghibli from bankruptcy. It was released during the time when Ghibli was dealing with financial strain , and probably would have had to close down if it flopped. Luckily, Princess Mononoke became a massive hit after its premiere, and it's loved among fans even now.

While the  anime remake by Science SARU  is one of the best anime series of the year, the legacy of the original film is impossible to beat. Directed by the legendary Mamoru Oshii, the  Ghost in the Shell  film is a pioneer of new animation techniques, known for its stunning visuals through the use of a blend of traditional cel animation with early computer-generated imagery. The movie isn't a faithful adaptation of the manga by Masamune Shirow, unlike the 2026 reboot, but it has its own charms. The movie took a much darker tone than the original manga, especially with the protagonist Motoko Kusanagi.

While she appeared much more cheerful in the manga, her personality in the movie suited the intense themes in the movie, especially considering its futuristic setting. Set in the year 2029, Major Motoko Kusanagi, a cyborg agent in Japan’s elite Public Security Section 9, is tasked with tracking down a mysterious hacker who hijacks cyborg brains through the internet. However, she never would have imagined that her search for the hacker would bring her closer to the truth behind the cyborg world, which blurs the lines between humans and machines.

If we're talking about timeless 1990s classics, we can't leave out this masterpiece by director Shinichirō Watanabe. Thanks to its space western themes, striking visuals, fluid action sequences, and jazz soundtrack, the series stood the test of time and remains one of the most beloved anime even now. The striking visuals are appreciated even more now since it’s virtually impossible to recreate them anymore. Aside from the visuals, Cowboy Bebop is often praised for its flawed characters and the tragic undertones.

Not only that, but the English dub surpassed even the original version , making it even more popular in the West. The story takes place in the year 2071, when humanity has spread across the galaxy, and the increase in crimes is causing an era of unrest. The only people capable of stopping these criminals are space bounty hunters, including those aboard the spaceship Bebop. While the story begins as a space adventure, it takes a drastic turn as it explores the protagonist’s complex past that comes back to haunt him.

Do you agree with our picks – or have an anime in mind that you want to add here? Share your recommendations in the comments below.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google For the first time since its initial teaser, Spyro: A Realm Beyond is likely to get new information during the 2026 Game Awards, giving players a better glimpse into the upcoming action platformer. This anticipated title is the first follow-up to the Spyro series in decades, after high-quality remasters invigorated the franchise with new life back in 2018. After showing off similarly sharp and polished visuals to the remastered trilogy back in June 2026, A Realm Beyond 's actual gameplay or release date might be the topic of its next reveal.

The primary look for Spyro: A Realm Beyond was completely cinematic CGI, meaning that it may not even represent the gameplay of the title when it releases. On its Steam page, A Realm Beyond is said to take place in a completely new world to the Spyro universe, where the confident purple dragon is stranded somewhere unfamiliar. By flying high and going through high-speed platforming to fight off new enemies called Scavs, Spyro needs to try to find their way home as they meet allies to help them around their journey.

An email sent to the team at ComicBook promised new information about Spyro: A Realm Beyond coming to The Game Awards (TGA) this year, as well as a reminder about what November means to the series. The first Spyro the Dragon for the original PlayStation was released in September 1998, marking almost three decades since the last stand-alone game in the series. Some assets for the newest game in the franchise were shared in Xbox's 25th Anniversary magazine, showing off small snippets and still images of A Realm Beyond gameplay that players haven't seen so far.

According to the marketing team behind the Spyro games currently, our email stated that "Who is ready to see more of the first all-new Spyro adventure in nearly 20 years? Sheep Beware." This comes after another statement saying that "The TGAs are around the corner, and Spyro is getting fired up." Both of these are almost direct confirmations that Spyro: A Realm Beyond gameplay featured in Xbox's Anniversary magazine will be shared with a larger audience at the event through a promotional trailer of some kind. This could be a longer cinematic trailer to take a deeper look at the game's story, but hopefully, some extended gameplay segments will also be shown.

Although some of the original creators of Spyro the Dragon aren't working on A Realm Beyond , the game's scale is set to be impressive from early hints. The teases in the Xbox magazine and the small gameplay pieces from the title's Steam page show a much grander, larger Spyro project than the franchise has gotten before. Classic gameplay ideas combined with a new art style and a more cinematic direction could revitalize the series, bringing in audiences who are unfamiliar with the classic PlayStation IP. Developer Toys for Bob clearly has a lot planned for the TGA event, but exactly what, we aren't too sure.

The two biggest pieces of information that could come out of this tease for the newest Spyro games are either a release date or a detailed gameplay breakdown for the title. A blog going through the first level or two of the game is less likely, but having any extended footage of the project will give players a much better idea of how A Realm Beyond is an evolution of the series rather than a retread. This is the first time the Spyro the Dragon franchise is officially continuing on its own, instead of going back to old games through remasters or having Spyro show up as a cameo in other titles.

So far, A Realm Beyond is slated for an "Early 2027" release window for the PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2, and PC. That being said, this is mostly through fan rumors rather than anything specific, with players estimating that February or March 2027 are relative timelines that would make sense. With the Painted Plains area of the new Spyro title from the Xbox magazine being part of the tease, expansions from that sneak peak could show where the actual release window is falling. Developers might share an Early, Mid, or Late 2027 release, but it's hard to imagine it wouldn't come out at some point next year.

The action platformer has a chance to become a definitive edition of the series, transforming it from an experimental PlayStation title into something more in-tune to modern gameplay design. In fact, this game has the chance to be the best Spyro game yet, taking all the best ideas from the nostalgic classics and building off them to produce something new. December 2026 is now even more excited for fans, as this latest tease from Spyro: A Realm Beyond 's developers promises a strong start of marketing for the title.

articles.title: 'GTA VI' Industry Domination Will Not End Anytime Soon
articles.summary: Without even having a PC launch date or a 'Grand Theft Auto Online' announcement, Rockstar Games has sold more than 17 million copies of its (latest) masterpiece.
articles.content:
If you're just waking up from a coma, we've got good news. If you've been in the coma since 2013, we've got really good news.

After 13 years and what has felt like as many delays, Grand Theft Auto VI comes out on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S at midnight (your local time). Finally . Pre-launch, GTA VI is already a smash hit, approaching $1.7 billion in pre-sales (and more than 17 million units sold), according to Sensor Tower data. It is also getting perfect review scores .

Yes, Rockstar is feeling like rockstars.

Probably no single piece of media has been as highly anticipated as GTA VI , developed and published by Take-Two Interactive imprint Rockstar Games . Some of the excitement is measurable. Last week, GTA VI ranked number one on Screen Engine/ASI's "Global Attention Share" chart, claiming 5.64 percent of the pie and booting Minecraft out of the spot it held for 45 straight weeks. It was the first time an unreleased game reach first place. Actually, it was the first time an unreleased game ranked better than fourth place (2019's Call of Duty: Modern Warfare ).

GTA VI has now spent 15 weeks in the international research firm's global top 10, obliterating Modern Warfare 's record of three weeks. ( Screen Engine/ASI balances Google search volume, Twitch and YouTube traffic, and Steam activity to arrive at a proprietary percentage of attention across thousands of games; tracking began in 2019.)

Colan Neese, Screen Engine/ASI's senior vice president of gaming, tells The Hollywood Reporter he expects GTA VI 's Global Attention Share will exceed 10 percent when the current week's numbers come out on Tuesday, Nov. 24. Neese predicts GTA VI will occupy his top spot through at least January 2027.

Gene Park, the digital culture and video games critic for The Washington Post , has already beaten Grand Theft Auto VI . It took him 55 hours of gameplay. (Park and select other reviewers received preview codes — and serious NDAs — from Rockstar.)

But there is so much more for Park in the seemingly endless playground that is Vice City: GTA VI 's setting based on real-life Miami. Park has since tacked on another 115 hours of gameplay, and is in no way bored.

When we spoke on Wednesday, Park was in the middle of a second full run through the game. This time, he is deliberately making different choices for the protagonists Jason and Lucia. The diverse results, Park says, have been staggering. (Also, he just discovered a zoo after 170 hours of gameplay — that should give you a sense of GTA VI 's sheer scale.)

There are "just two ways" GTA VI "could have disappointed," Joost van Dreunen, a video-game industry strategist and NYU professor, told THR . The first would have taken "some kind of awful geopolitical event." Boy does it feel like we came close during this past week. The second is series of crippling bugs a la Cyberpunk 2077 . Rockstar would have never let that happen, van Dreunen said. The publisher would have just delayed GTA VI a third time.

As it is, GTA VI is awesome. After a baker's-dozen years and an $80-$100 price tag, it had to be. The anticipation (and those delays) has created a "novel… simultaneous synchronized event" experience for a single-player video game, van Dreunen said, which was not possible prior to the digital age. (Rockstar is not releasing GTA VI discs.)

Park believes it will be "a couple of months at the very least" before we get an Online option. GTA V 's Online component still brings in $300-$500 million per year in revenue, per van Dreunen, through Shark Cash Cards . (You pay real money for in-game currency; Grand Theft Auto Online launched just two weeks after GTA V .)

Van Dreunen says GTA VI will be the dominant video game for "easily" a year, and probably longer. Its coming (but not announced) PC launch and inevitable GTA Online integration (also not announced) will keep the champagne corks popping like, well, Rockstar's parent company's stock. Shares of Take-Two Interactive's Software (TTWO) are up more than 7 percent (from Tuesday's market close) on those glowing GTA VI reviews — and Wednesday was a down day for the major index funds.

GTA VI officially releases on Thursday. Completely unrelated, boss, I feel a cold coming on…

articles.title: GTA 6 Removes a Major GTA 5 Feature, But the Reasoning Makes Sense
articles.summary: Courtesy of Rockstar Games Grand Theft Auto 6 has made a significant change to one of Rockstar Games' familiar features, as players cannot revisit completed story missions through a dedicated in-game replay menu. The feature has been a regular part of the developer's recent releases, giving players the freedom to return to memorable moments, experiment with different approaches, or […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Grand Theft Auto 6 has made a significant change to one of Rockstar Games' familiar features, as players cannot revisit completed story missions through a dedicated in-game replay menu. The feature has been a regular part of the developer's recent releases, giving players the freedom to return to memorable moments, experiment with different approaches, or simply experience their favorite missions again. However, the latest entry takes a different approach, and its branching narrative may be the reason.

According to IGN , whose reviewer completed a full playthrough of the game, GTA 6 does not include a dedicated option for replaying story missions. This marks a stark departure from previous Rockstar releases, which have generally allowed players to revisit completed missions after finishing them. While the studio hasn't directly commented on the omission, the game's interconnected storytelling offers a likely explanation for the decision.

The biggest consideration appears to be how decisions made throughout GTA 6 's story can influence events much later in the adventure. Certain missions can unfold in dramatically different ways depending on choices players have made hours earlier. Even decisions that might initially seem insignificant can affect how Jason and Lucia approach later situations, creating outcomes that aren't necessarily the same for every player.

This makes the traditional mission replay system considerably more complicated. Allowing players to revisit a completed mission independently could create inconsistencies with the events that have already unfolded in their particular playthrough. A mission that originally ended with a relatively straightforward outcome might play out very differently when approached again, potentially undermining the consequences of earlier decisions. The same interconnected storytelling also extends into open-world encounters, where seemingly spontaneous events can be influenced by previous actions.

It's worth emphasizing that this is a possible explanation for the design decision rather than a direct statement from Rockstar. Nevertheless, it offers a plausible reason for why the studio might have decided to leave the familiar feature behind as it builds a more reactive version of its open world.

Players aren't completely without options entirely, however. GTA 6 includes additional manual save slots that can be used, meaning players can preserve their progress at important points throughout the campaign and return to those moments by loading an earlier save. It requires a little more preparation than selecting a completed mission from a menu, but it does provide a way to revisit certain parts of the story.

Whether Rockstar eventually introduces a dedicated replay feature remains unknown. For now, players will have to approach GTA 6 's story missions as part of a continuous adventure rather than individual experiences they can freely revisit.

articles.title: 'Sentimental Value' Casting Guru Recalls Meta Stellan Skarsgard and Elle Fanning Experience
articles.summary: Yngvill Haga also discussed her rapport with Joachim Trier and Fanning's Oscar nomination during an appearance in the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival's market program.
articles.content:
You may not know Yngvill Haga by name. But the likes of Stellan Skarsgard and her regular collaborator Joachim Trier do. And you very likely know the Norwegian's work as a casting director on the likes of Trier's Oscar winner Sentimental Value , The Worst Person in the World and Thelma .

On Wednesday, she took the spotlight, of sorts, herself in an appearance at the Industry@Tallinn & Baltic Event (ITBE) , the market of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF) in Estonia, whose 30th edition runs through this weekend. Asked about how she first met Trier, Haga shared: "His producer at that time texted or called me. 'Do you want to have a coffee with him?' I didn't know him, and I always want to meet directors that I don't know, so yeah, sure. I don't know who has seen Sentimental Value , but we met at Lorry's, the restaurant where the father and daughter have this talk [in the film]. Joachim loves that place, and he pitched me for a film called Thelma ." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The casting expert not only liked the film but also their connection. "I immediately liked his pitch and also our way of communicating, talking together," Haga said. "He hadn't worked with a casting director before; he had put people together to do his casting, but now he wanted to try out something else, and so it started from there."

Of course, Trier wrote Sentimental Value with Renate Reinsve in mind. "When I first met Joachim [about the film], he pitched the story again, and he said, in a kind of nervous way, 'I'm starting to think about Stellan Skarsgard.' He didn't know him and had never worked with him, but had such huge respect." Trier went to Stockholm and met the star, who then came on board. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Had Haga known the Swedish actor personally before Sentimental Value ? "No, I met him during this process," she noted.

The casting director also shared insight into how Elle Fanning ended up in the film and took her first trip to Oslo. "We worked with an American casting director, Avy Kaufman, and Joachim has an agent in the U.S. who, of course, knows all the big acting agents," Haga explained why she wasn't directly involved.

"I was talking to Joachim and saying who I liked, and I was super happy that it ended up being Elle Fanning — for many reasons," she continued. The facts that she is a bit younger than the sisters and is blonde, while the sisters are dark-haired, already helped. "It's just a very visually cool contrast," Haga argued. "And I know that some of the actresses [Trier] was talking to didn't like the role and didn't want it because it wasn't the lead. I personally really like her character, so I thought that was very strange. And Elle Fanning was like nothing like that. She saw the importance of the role and liked the role. Also, she got Oscar-nominated, so she was very grateful and moved."

Haga also recalled Fanning's first visit to Oslo to do fittings and rehearsals. "The house that's in the film is a house in Oslo that they had rented for half a year or so," she said. "The rehearsals in the film are happening in the house where he's filming, and we also did the rehearsals in the house, and they asked me to read the other female parts of the scenes. So that was cool for me to be part of a scene with Stellan and Elle, and that was the first time I met her. But it was so meta because we were rehearsing a rehearsal scene and doing it on the location, and she had come over from the U.S., which was her first time in Oslo — like her character. So it was super weird, but very fun."

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google PS5 users across the internet have been left baffled and frustrated that the PlayStation Network has been experiencing issues just before the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 . With the U.S. and European releases of GTA 6 now less than 12 hours away, many are beginning to boot up their PS5 in anticipation of jumping into the world of Leonida the moment that they can. Unfortunately, these plans seem to have been disrupted for some, which has resulted in many GTA fans beginning to panic.

Across social media, PlayStation users have been expressing disbelief that PSN is having struggles at such a pivotal moment. Not only is Grand Theft Auto 6 the biggest game to release on PS5 (or any platform) in 2026, but its arrival has been 13 years in the making, following the launch of GTA 5 in 2013. For PSN to now be having difficulties just before GTA 6 goes live could prevent millions from being able to play the game on PS5 after well over a decade of anticipation.

"I’ve had [ Grand Theft Auto 6 ] pre-loaded, but I’m guessing I will need to get connected tomorrow to get it unlocked. Y’all better not screw this up for me," said user skarr220 on Reddit .

"We waited 13 years for a digital version of GTA 6 just for PSN to be down on release date," @DrClown21 said of the issue.

"Imagine how mad people are gonna be if all their PTO gets wasted by PSN being down," added @TimmyTangoVT on X.

The good news with this matter is that this PSN outage doesn't seem to be impacting every PlayStation user around the globe. Countless PS5 owners have made it known that online services for their own console continue to work without flaw. PlayStation's own status website continues to report that everything tied to PSN is functioning as it should as well, with no errors tied to the PS Store, account management, or sign-in said to be transpiring.

Whether or not this will continue to hold true as GTA 6 actually becomes available in the United States and various European countries, however, remains to be seen. As more people continue to download GTA 6 in these regions, there's always the possibility that PSN's servers could start to run into greater problems that would result in widespread outages. Hopefully, none of these fears will end up being realized, but it will be worth monitoring as midnight approaches and GTA 6 finally becomes available.

Have you had any PSN issues for yourself today? And how are you going to feel if PSN does end up running into problems right before Grand Theft Auto 6 unlocks on PS5? Let me know down in the comments section.

articles.title: Robert Downey Jr. Breaks Down His MCU Return in New Avengers: Doomsday Video, And Why He's Back
articles.summary: Image courtesy of Marvel Among the biggest shockers about Avengers: Doomsday was the news that Robert Downey Jr. would be returning to the MCU, and now, we are finally hearing more from Downey himself about why he's making this return, just one month ahead of Doomsday's release. There's no denying that Downey is one of the most iconic figures […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Among the biggest shockers about Avengers: Doomsday was the news that Robert Downey Jr. would be returning to the MCU, and now, we are finally hearing more from Downey himself about why he's making this return, just one month ahead of Doomsday's release. There's no denying that Downey is one of the most iconic figures in the entire MCU, not only because Iron Man was the film that started it all but also because Downey became perhaps the single biggest name in the entire franchise. It was therefore a surprise—and, frankly, a heart breaking one—when Avengers: Endgame suggested the ship had well and truly sailed on Downey's time with Marvel.

Of course, audiences now know that's not true, but that has only led to more questions. Whereas Chris Evans' return as Steve Rogers still has some questions related to what the implications of this return are, his appearance makes a fair bit of sense (especially now knowing that his decision to stay in the past caused Doomsday ). With Downey playing Doctor Doom, though, so many major questions remain, from whether Doom is a Tony Stark variant, which the Russo brothers have repeatedly denied , to whether there is someone else actually under the mask. In all likelihood, we won't get any major reveals until Doomsday his the big screen, but Downey has at least shared new insight into his choice to return. Check out his exact comments below.

In a new video shared by Marvel, Downey discusses his decision to return to the MCU, especially after feeling like his exit was definitive following Endgame . Among other things, in the video, Downey explains, "Any of these movies is only as good as its villain. Victor is a master manipulator, and because of that, there's levels to the stakes here." That alone suggests that we will be getting a Doctor Doom worthy of Downey's return, which he ultimately reinforced in this very same video, saying, "We just really keep trying to earn it with every breath." However, this goes beyond just hinting that the choice to bring Downey back will prove to be more than worth it. In fact, these details, along with the clip of the Downey as Doom reveal, in which Downey says, "New mask, same task," might contain some hints about what's to come.

For quite some time, there has been a theory running that Doom doesn't actually look like Tony Stark, whether that's a fake-out from Marvel itself with another actor really under the mask or another explanation, such as Victor just using his abilities to look like Tony in order to manipulate the Avengers. With Downey's comments about Victor being a master manipulator, that may be exactly where this plot is headed, although there is still, of course, no confirmation to that effect.

Additionally, though, highlighting Downey's previous "new mask, same task" comment seems most likely connected to the idea that Tony wanted "a suit of armor around the world," and Doom, in his own very likely misguided way, likewise thinks he is doing what he's doing to save the multiverse. Granted, there may be even more hints hidden in what Downey has said in this video, but these details alone should have audiences more than excited for the upcoming Avengers movie.

What's your theory for why Robert Downey Jr. was cast to play Doom and what that might mean for the Doomsday story? Let us know your thoughts in the comments down below.
